subtitle: Where Forest Rivers Met a Kadamba Crown

panels.shot: high, sweeping aerial wide over dense forest split by a looping river, a small stone town glinting at its bend
panels.action: Banavasi sprawls between dark forests and the curving Varada river, early stone shrines and timber halls clustered around a rising temple mound as morning mist curls over water and treetops.

dialogue.text: Between two forest rivers, an old shrine of Bhava became Banavasi, where Satakarni’s memory and Kadamba power fused into the first great capital of the Kannada land.

i18n.hi: दो जंगल नदियों के बीच, भाव के पुराने देवालय से बना बनवासी, जहाँ सातकर्णि की याद और कदंब ताकत मिलकर पहली बड़ी कन्नड़ राजधानी बनी।

panels.shot: slow push-in from sky to the sinuous bend of the Varada, emphasizing the natural amphitheatre of land
panels.action: From high above, the Varada curves like a silver serpent around a raised tongue of land, fields and groves hugging the banks while deep forest presses close beyond.

dialogue.text: Long before kings chose it for their throne, Banavasi was chosen by the land itself, a safe tongue of earth between the coiled arms of the Varada.

i18n.hi: राजाओं के सिंहासन से बहुत पहले, खुद भूमि ने चुना बनवासी को, वरदा की कुंडली बाँहों के बीच सुरक्षित जुबान-सी धरती।

panels.shot: ground-level wide of forest track meeting river ghat, caravans converging from different directions
panels.action: Merchants with pack-bulls and carts emerge from thick sal and bamboo, descending a worn path to a simple river ghat where boats are moored and villagers watch.

dialogue.text: Forest tracks from the western hills, the coastal plain and the Malnad met at this bend, where traders cooled their feet, and news moved faster than the river.

i18n.hi: पश्चिमी पहाड़, तटीय मैदानी और मलनाड से आती पगडंडियाँ यहीं मोड़ पर मिलतीं, जहाँ व्यापारी पाँव भिगोते, और खबर नदी से तेज बहती।

panels.shot: medium wide on a modest early shrine under a spreading tree, with river visible beyond
panels.action: A small stone platform with a roughly carved linga stands beneath a grand tree, oil lamps flickering as a priest offers flowers, while the Varada glimmers behind the shrine.

dialogue.text: Here, by the water and the tree, rose the shrine of Bhava, the fierce form of Shiva, tended by priests and kings whose names the forest almost forgot.

i18n.hi: यहीं, पेड़ और पानी के पास उठी भाव की देवगाह, शिव का उग्र रूप, जिसे जंगल-भूल से पुजारी और राजा संभालते रहे।

panels.shot: low-angle medium on a Satakarni-period king in simple crown, standing before the shrine
panels.action: An earlier Deccan king in satakarni-era garb stands in respectful pose before the Bhava shrine, hands joined, attendants with fly-whisks and parasol held back from the sanctum’s shadow.

dialogue.text: The Talagunda inscription remembers this place, saying Satakarni and other kings worshipped here, binding their fortunes to this small, fierce god on the riverbank.

i18n.hi: तलगुंडा की शिला याद रखती है इसे, बताती है कैसे सातकर्णि और दूसरे राजा यहाँ पूजते, अपनी किस्मत इस नदी किनारे के छोटे, उग्र देव से बाँधते।

panels.shot: time-lapse style wide, same shrine over centuries as surroundings subtly change
panels.action: The scene shows the shrine in the same spot while subtle shifts appear around it—older timber structures give way to sturdier stone, more huts gather near, yet the linga and tree remain constant.

dialogue.text: Empires rose and slipped away in the Deccan, but the Bhava temple stayed by the Varada, a fixed point around which new rulers learned the old paths.

i18n.hi: दक्खिन में साम्राज्य उठे और ढहे, पर भाव का देवालय वरदा किनारे अडिग रहा, वह धुरी बना, जिसके चारों ओर नए राजे पुराने रास्ते सीखते।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Banavasi region, with labels implied by landscape: hills, forests, routes
panels.action: Low hills ring the horizon, dense forest lies to the west, terraced fields climb from the river, and faint paths snake toward distant passes and unseen coasts.

dialogue.text: This was not an empty space for a new crown. Chutu chiefs and other satakarni lords had already threaded these woods, planted fields, and stamped their seals on this frontier.

i18n.hi: ये नई मुकुट के लिए खाली जगह न थी। चूटु सरदार और दूसरे सातकर्णि नरेश पहले ही इन जंगलों से गुज़रे, खेत जोते, और इस सीमा पर अपनी मुहरें गाड़ गए थे।

panels.shot: medium shot of a group of local elites and brahmanas gathered under a tree, scrolls and palm leaves in hand
panels.action: Local landholders and brahmanas sit under shade, palm-leaf records spread out, pointing toward the shrine and the river as they speak with measured gestures.

dialogue.text: Banavasi’s strength lay in more than stone. It lay in land grants, old sanctuaries, and networks of priests and chiefs whose loyalties could make or unmake a capital.

i18n.hi: बनवासी की ताकत सिर्फ पत्थर में न थी। वह थी भूमि दान, पुराने देवस्थानों, और उन पुजारियों–सरदारों के जाल में, जिनकी वफादारी राजधानी बना भी सकती थी, मिटा भी।

panels.shot: slow push-in on the Bhava shrine transformed into a more formal temple complex, with early stone mantapa
panels.action: The once-modest shrine now stands within a square stone courtyard, with a simple mantapa and gateway; villagers, soldiers and officials converge toward it from different lanes.

dialogue.text: When Mayurasharma and his Kadamba line chose Banavasi, they did not build upon a blank page. They crowned what was already sacred, letting old stones carry new names.

i18n.hi: जब मयूरशर्मा और उनकी कदंब वंश ने बनवासी चुना, उन्होंने सफ़ा कागज़ पर नहीं लिखा। उन्होंने पहले से पवित्र जगह को मुकुट दिया, पुराने पत्थरों पर नए नाम चढ़ा दिए।

panels.shot: medium low-angle of a Kadamba king in courtly dress entering the temple precinct with retinue
panels.action: A Kadamba king in early 5th-century Deccan attire ascends the temple steps with measured dignity, retinue behind, as villagers watch from the sides of the stone courtyard.

dialogue.text: The Kadambas made Banavasi their Vaijayanti, their banner of victory. Their court rose beside Bhava’s shrine, binding royal ritual to village memory and river trade.

i18n.hi: कदंबों ने बनवासी को अपना वैजयंती बनाया, विजय का ध्वज। उनका दरबार भाव मंदिर के पास उठा, जहाँ राजकर्म, गाँव की याद और नदी व्यापार, सब एक धागे में बँधे।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye of the growing town: palace compound, temple, tanks, streets between river arms
panels.action: From above, an organized town spreads between the arms of the Varada—palace enclosure, temple complex, stepped tanks, straight streets and markets radiating from the sacred core.

dialogue.text: Under Kadamba hands, the landscape thickened. Tanks were dug, streets traced the curve of the river, and a royal court took shape between the temple and the water.

i18n.hi: कदंब हाथों से ये भू-दृश्य घना हो उठा। तालाब खुदे, गलियाँ नदी की मोड़ के साथ मुड़ीं, और मंदिर व पानी के बीच एक राजदरबार आकार लेने लगा।

panels.shot: medium wide of workers constructing a large tank, with a dignified overseer pointing toward the temple and river
panels.action: Laborers line up baskets of soil to build the walls of a broad tank, while a royal official gestures, aligning the new reservoir with both the temple tower and the river’s course.

dialogue.text: In Talagunda, the inscription recalls Kakusthavarma and his tank. Such waters were not just for thirst—they mirrored the sky, fed fields, and anchored kingly merit in stone and earth.

i18n.hi: तलगुंडा की शिला ककुत्स्तवर्मन और उनके तालाब को गिनती है। ऐसी जलाशय सिर्फ प्यास के लिए न थे—वे आकाश का अक्स, खेतों की जान, और राजा के पुण्य को मिट्टी–पत्थर में बाँधने का साधन थे।

panels.shot: close-up on the calm surface of a tank reflecting temple and sky, with faint ripples
panels.action: The still surface of a stepped tank reflects the temple doorway and a slice of sky; a single leaf drifts, its movement sending small rings across the mirrored tower.

dialogue.text: If the Varada carried Banavasi’s trade, these tanks held its seasons. They turned rain into prestige, and everyday water into a visible sign of royal care.

i18n.hi: यदि वरदा बनवासी का व्यापार ढोती थी, तो ये तालाब उसके मौसम सँभालते थे। वे बारिश को प्रतिष्ठा बनाते, रोज़मर्रा के पानी को राज–पालन का दिखता निशान।

panels.shot: medium of a scribe carving letters on a stone pillar, temple and river glimpsed behind
panels.action: A scribe crouches by a tall pillar, carefully incising neat Brahmi letters with a chisel, as the temple roofline and glinting river form the distant backdrop.

dialogue.text: Inscriptions cut into stone tied these waters and shrines to names: Satakarni, Kadamba, Kakusthavarma. They fixed the meeting of old devotion and new dynasty in scripts that outlived both.

i18n.hi: पत्थर पर खुदी लेखनाओं ने इन जलाशयों और देवालयों को बाँधा नामों से: सातकर्णि, कदंब, ककुत्स्तवर्मन। उन्होंने पुरानी भक्ति और नई राजवंश के मिलन को ऐसी लिपि में जकड़ दिया जो दोनों से लंबी चली।

panels.shot: wide showing both palace and temple, with mixed crowd of warriors, merchants, brahmanas and villagers
panels.action: Between the palace walls and the temple courtyard, a busy lane seethes with armored guards, robed brahmanas, women with pots, and traders leading animals, all framed by river gleams at the edges.

dialogue.text: Power in Banavasi did not flow from the palace alone. It flowed along this lane, where warrior, merchant and priest moved between court and shrine, all under the same river light.

i18n.hi: बनवासी में ताकत सिर्फ महल से न बहती। वो इसी गली से बहती, जहाँ वीर, व्यापारी और पुजारी, दरबार और देवालय के बीच आते–जाते, सब एक ही नदी उजाले में।

panels.shot: subtle time-shift wide: the core temple remains, but surrounding architecture shows later Chalukya touches
panels.action: The central linga shrine stands as before, but the hall around it bears more ornate pillars and carved details, hinting at Early and Later Chalukya hands layered onto the old core.

dialogue.text: Centuries later, new dynasties refaced Banavasi’s sacred heart. The Madhukeshvara temple we see now is a palimpsest—Kadamba foundations bearing Chalukya carvings, old Bhava beneath later stone.

i18n.hi: सदियों बाद, नए वंशों ने बनवासी के पवित्र हृदय को फिर से गढ़ा। आज का मधुकेश्वर मंदिर एक पलिम्प्सेस्ट है—कदंब नींव पर चालुक्य नक्काशी, बाद की चट्टानों के नीचे पुराना भाव।

panels.shot: medium of a much later pilgrim looking up at the temple tower, while monks and pilgrims move beyond
panels.action: A later-age pilgrim in simple robes stands at the edge of the courtyard, gazing up at the temple tower, as other visitors and a few monks pass by toward different shrines in the distance.

dialogue.text: By Xuanzang’s time, the wider region held many monasteries, many faiths. But his road too passed near this old capital, which had taught the land how a river town could be a seat of rule.

i18n.hi: ह्वेनसांग के ज़माने तक, विस्तृत भूभाग में अनेक विहार, अनेक मत थे। पर उसकी राह भी इस पुरानी राजधानी के पास से गुज़री, जिसने देश को सिखाया कि नदी नगर भी राजगद्दी हो सकता है।

panels.shot: evening wide of modern Banavasi’s Madhukeshvara complex and surrounding village by the river, in warm light
panels.action: In soft evening light, the current Madhukeshvara temple rises over tiled village houses, with the Varada flowing quietly beside fields and trees, smoke from small cooking fires curling upward.

dialogue.text: Today, Banavasi seems a quiet temple town. Yet every stone lane and tank holds the memory of when this bend in the Varada was the nerve of a young Kannada kingdom.

i18n.hi: आज बनवासी एक शांत देवनगर लगता है। फिर भी हर पत्थर गली और हर तालाब में वो याद है, जब वरदा का यह मोड़ नवयुवा कन्नड़ राज्य की नसें था।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from close-up of the river’s edge to a wide where temple, town and forest frame the water
panels.action: The camera pulls back from ripples on the Varada at dawn to reveal the temple gopura, clustered houses and dark forest beyond, all held together by the looping river.

dialogue.text: Banavasi teaches that a capital endures when it grows from the land’s own grain—where river, road and remembered shrine meet, power can rise, fall, and still leave a living trace.

i18n.hi: बनवासी सिखाता है कि राजधानी तभी टिकती है, जब वह मिट्टी की अपनी बनावट से उगे—जहाँ नदी, राह और याद किया देवालय मिलें, वहाँ सत्ता उठ–गिर कर भी ज़िंदा निशान छोड़ती है।

subtitle_i18n.en: Where Forest Rivers Met a Kadamba Crown
subtitle_i18n.hi: जहाँ जंगल की नदियाँ मिलीं कदंब मुकुट से
